title: Number of Ways to Paint Sheets
summary: Given an integer n for the number of sheets, and an array limit of size m indicating the maximum sheets that can be painted with each color, find the number of ways to paint all sheets using exactly two distinct colors, each covering a contiguous segment, without exceeding the limit for each color.
statement: Given an integer n for the number of sheets, and an array limit of size m indicating the maximum sheets that can be painted with each color, find the number of ways to paint all sheets using exactly two distinct colors, each covering a contiguous segment, without exceeding the limit for each color. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7. Different ways are those where at least one sheet is painted differently.
constraints: 2≤n≤10^9 and there are up to 100,000 colors.
Use exactly two distinct colors, each on one nonempty contiguous segment.
Color i may cover at most limit[i] sheets; return ordered paintings modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Cap every color at n-1 because both segments must be nonempty.
For ordered capacities a and b, valid splits count max(0,a+b-n+1).
Sort capacities; for each a, binary-search the suffix with b≥n-a and sum the linear expression using prefix sums, then remove the same-color term.
Every painting has a unique ordered color pair and split, so summing this exact count covers each valid painting once.

tests.explanation: Across ordered color pairs, six split positions satisfy both capacity limits.
Either color may come first and either split position works, giving four.
